title: Clover\-35B\-A3B\-Preview: A New Way for Intelligence
gist: DiffuSpace released Clover-35B-A3B-Preview, an open (Apache) 35B-total/3B-active MoE diffusion language model claiming to beat the similarly sized autoregressive Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on agentic benchmarks while generating far faster (680 tokens/s on one GB300). It also previews a Clover-based decision model with a parallel Joint Mode; all numbers are vendor-reported.

insights.claim: DiffuSpace claims its 35B-total, 3B-active MoE diffusion language model Clover-35B-A3B-Preview outperforms the similarly sized autoregressive Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on multiple benchmarks while generating significantly faster.
insights.speaker: DiffuSpace Core Team
insights.so_what: Evidence that diffusion LLMs can match autoregressive quality at scale would challenge the autoregressive default in inference-cost and latency planning; benchmarks are vendor-reported and a Preview.
insights.quote: Speed and performance can coexist in a single model.

insights.claim: The Dream model family from the University of Hong Kong NLP Group (Dream 7B, April 2025) has passed 2.7 million Hugging Face downloads, and members of that team founded DiffuSpace to build on it.
insights.speaker: DiffuSpace Core Team
insights.so_what: Shows real open-source traction for diffusion LLMs and the academic-to-startup pipeline behind Clover.

insights.claim: Clover's gains are attributed to a redesigned Bidirectional Gated DeltaNet for Block Diffusion, with history compressed into the recurrent state and fine-grained bidirectional softmax attention inside the current block.
insights.speaker: DiffuSpace Core Team
insights.so_what: Linear-attention hybrids adapted to block-parallel denoising are the architectural path to watch for fast diffusion LLMs.

insights.claim: The Clover design lets the model learn when to rely on historical context versus the current block, using a readout from historical memory in the same softmax as in-block tokens, learnable block-size calibration, and a zero-initialized right-side convolution branch.
insights.speaker: DiffuSpace Core Team
insights.so_what: Concrete architectural recipe other labs may copy or benchmark against.

insights.claim: Clover-35B-A3B-Preview scores 73.6 on SWE-bench Verified, 51.7 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 65.3 on tau3 Overall, and tops all six agent benchmarks in the authors' comparison against LLaDA2.2 flash, Mercury 2.5, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B.
insights.speaker: DiffuSpace Core Team
insights.so_what: Agentic-coding strength in a 3B-active model matters for cheap agent serving; verify independently since the comparison set is chosen by the vendor.

insights.claim: On general benchmarks Clover scores 83.8 on GPQA Diamond, 95.8 on ZebraLogic and 72.0 on AA-LCR, matching or exceeding similarly sized autoregressive models.
insights.speaker: DiffuSpace Core Team
insights.so_what: Suggests no major general-capability penalty from the diffusion approach at this size.

insights.claim: Clover reaches 680 tokens/s on internal agent workloads on a single NVIDIA GB300 (BF16, batch size 1), and 515 tokens/s on an H200 versus 365 tokens/s for a Qwen model accelerated with DFlash2.
insights.speaker: DiffuSpace Core Team
insights.so_what: A roughly 1.4x speed edge over an optimized autoregressive baseline on H200 is the core commercial claim; watch for third-party replication.

insights.claim: Because agents loop through decide-execute-feedback cycles, generation latency compounds, so faster decoding lets agents explore more paths in the same time.
insights.speaker: DiffuSpace Core Team
insights.so_what: Inference speed is positioned as a capability multiplier for agent products, not just a cost lever.
insights.quote: For AI agents, speed is itself a core capability.

insights.claim: In a 49-task WebMCP evaluation with three attempts per task, Clover's median agent execution time is 1.52 seconds versus 8.86 seconds for Gemini3.6 Flash.
insights.speaker: DiffuSpace Core Team
insights.so_what: A roughly 6x latency gap against a proprietary flash model, if it holds, is a notable competitive claim for interactive agents.
insights.locator: WebMCP: Completing Six Business Tasks in Sequence

insights.claim: Clover runs with INT4 quantization on a 16GB RTX 5070 Ti at 101.8 tokens/s on MATH-500, versus 48.5 tokens/s for similarly sized MiniCPM and Qwen models.
insights.speaker: DiffuSpace Core Team
insights.so_what: A 35B-class agentic model on a consumer 16GB GPU expands the edge-inference market; watch consumer GPU and local-inference demand.

insights.claim: Against MiniCPM-V 4.7, LFM2.5, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning and Gemma 4, Clover wins six of nine benchmarks and beats the same-configuration MiniCPM-V 4.7 by 15.7 points on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 28.0 on SWE-bench Verified.
insights.speaker: DiffuSpace Core Team
insights.so_what: Positions Clover as best-in-class for efficient open models, pressuring other small-MoE vendors.

insights.claim: DiffuSpace will release a Clover-based decision model with a Joint Mode that answers up to eight related questions in parallel within one denoising process, letting answers inform each other and avoid logical conflicts.
insights.speaker: DiffuSpace Core Team
insights.so_what: Parallel generation is a natural fit for structured multi-question judgments, an emerging product niche for diffusion models.

insights.claim: On an internal set of 500 groups and 2,420 related questions, Joint Mode got 95.0% of questions right and 80.4% of groups fully right, versus 89.8% and 62.4% in Independent Mode and 63.6% and 15.8% for TypeSafe's Jev.
insights.speaker: DiffuSpace Core Team
insights.so_what: Large claimed edge over Jev but on an internal validation set with Jev numbers from historical evaluations, so treat cautiously.

insights.claim: Joint Mode lets correlated judgments, such as contract notice timeliness and deposit retention, be generated concurrently, reducing inconsistent answer combinations that independent calls can produce.
insights.speaker: DiffuSpace Core Team
insights.so_what: Consistency across dependent decisions matters for legal and compliance automation use cases.
insights.locator: The Same Contract, Five Correlated Judgments

insights.claim: Clover is released open source under an Apache license with weights on Hugging Face and ModelScope, code on GitHub, and inference support in SGLang and llama.cpp; Qwen architectures were the starting point for the research.
insights.speaker: DiffuSpace Core Team
insights.so_what: Permissive licensing plus mainstream runtime support lowers adoption friction for diffusion LLMs.

insights.claim: SigmaZ is DiffuSpace's exclusive GenUI ecosystem partner for education, and joint post-training aims to raise throughput to 2,000 tokens per second.
insights.speaker: DiffuSpace Core Team
insights.so_what: A 2,000 tokens/s target signals the speed trajectory DiffuSpace is pursuing, with education as the first vertical.

insights.claim: DiffuSpace is developing an agent execution harness and a desktop coding client to be rolled out shortly, alongside multimodal, long-horizon stability and edge adaptation work.
insights.speaker: DiffuSpace Core Team
insights.so_what: Moving up-stack into agent tooling suggests DiffuSpace aims to compete on products, not only open weights.
